title: Child Protective Service's Procedures for Suspected Child Abuse Cases Reported by Schools
what_it_is: Child Protective Service's Procedures for Suspected Child Abuse Cases Reported by Schools

sections.label: CPS powers threshold
sections.summary: CPS powers require reasonable grounds to believe a child is in need of care or protection; not attending school alone is insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The threshold for CPS to exercise various powers under the Act is predicated on whether there are "reasonable grounds to believe that a child or young person is in need of care or protection".

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The fact that a child is not attending school is not, by itself, sufficient grounds to invoke CYPA powers.

sections.label: CPS in-person assessment powers
sections.summary: CPS conducts in-person assessments for immediate safety concerns or uncooperative parents, and may order assessments, treatments, or removal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: If the assessment is that there is immediate or serious safety concerns for the child, or when parents or caregivers are uncooperative, CPS will conduct an in-person assessment of the child and the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: CPS may also order a child to undergo assessments, examinations or treatments, or remove the child and commit him or her to a place of temporary care and protection or to the care of a fit person.

sections.label: NAVH helpline reporting channel
sections.summary: With investigations ongoing, MSF launched an online text-based channel via its website as an additional NAVH reporting mode.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: As investigations for the case are currently ongoing, we cannot comment on the specific details, but I do agree on the need for us to work harder collectively to make sure that the NAVH helpline and other sources of assistance are made known to those who might be in need of such assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And on that matter, just in December last year, MSF launched an online text-based channel that is accessible via MSF's website as an additional mode of reporting for NAVH to make it easier for reporting.

sections.label: CPS in-person assessment phase
sections.summary: CPS officers can proceed to in-person assessment if a child's safety is at risk or parents are uncooperative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: If we find that there are instances where the child's safety is immediately found to be at risk, or if the parents are uncooperative such that the CPS officers do not get to sight the child, then the CPS officer has every right to move on to the next phase to conduct an in-person assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Specific to Mr Gerald Giam's question on whether there were examples of such cases in the past five years, I will encourage him to file a separate Parliamentary Question on this if he would like to ask for the specific statistics, because I do not have them at the moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Again, rest assured that the CPS officers, given their procedures, have the ability to step in if there is an assessed need to do so.
